## What an applicant tracking system is, and what changes past 500 people
An applicant tracking system (ATS) is the one place where the hiring actually happens: the job, the candidates, the stages they move through, the interviews, the decisions and the record that is left afterwards. When it works, a recruiter opens one board in the morning and knows who is waiting for whom. When it does not, the real process lives in a spreadsheet, an inbox and the memory of one person who is on holiday.
This guide is about the category, written by a company that makes one. Where we describe how something works, we describe how it works in Teamtailor and say so. Where a requirement applies to every vendor, we say that too.

### Five things that change
Below a few hundred employees, one team can agree on one way of hiring. Past a few hundred people that stops being possible, and the system has to carry the differences instead of flattening them. Five things change.
- Several legal entities and brands. A candidate applying to the hotel in Lisbon should land on that brand's career site, not on the group's.
- Several countries. Each has its own privacy rules, retention periods and, in some, a works council that wants to see how candidate data is handled before anyone signs.
- Volume. One role that draws four hundred applications makes the shared inbox impossible, and the thread with the hiring manager that two people are copied on and one of them reads stops being a joke.
- Governance. Who may publish a job, who may see salary data, who approved the requisition, and who can prove it a year later.
- Procurement. A security questionnaire, a data processing agreement (DPA), sometimes a legal review in two languages.
The requirements in this guide are set at the bar a company of 1,000+ employees applies. They serve the smaller buyer as well, who will meet the same questions a little later.
Prices, certificates and legal dates change. Every figure in this guide carries a marker that points to the source list at the end of the page, and the dates are the ones the sources gave on 20 October 2026.

## How an ATS works, step by step
The clearest way to see what an ATS does is to follow one role from request to first day. This is how that runs in Teamtailor. Other systems order things differently, but the same seven jobs have to be done somewhere.

### 1. The requisition and the ad
The role starts as a request, and the approval happens inside the system, not in a mail thread. A hiring manager submits the job as pending, a recruiter or an approver releases it, and the trail shows who said yes. The ad is drafted from a few lines about the role and then edited by a person. One publish sends it to the career site and the job boards, and the career site itself is built inside the ATS, so the ad, the form and the pipeline share one set of data.
At scale, the approval chain is where the enterprise angle sits: a requisition for a role in one country may need a finance sign-off, while the same role elsewhere does not. The system has to hold both.

### 2. The applications
People apply without creating an account, and they do it from a phone, often on the bus. Someone who is not ready to apply can connect instead, leaving contact details so the team can come back when a fitting role opens. Both routes end up as candidates on the same board, which is what makes the talent pool worth anything later.

### 3. Screening
Screening questions are set per job: right to work, a licence, shift availability, a language. Triggers then do the routine part. A trigger can move a candidate to a stage, send a message or prompt a recruiter to look, depending on how the team set it up. What is automatic is what the team configured, and nothing else.

### 4. Stages and the people in them
Every candidate sits on one board, in a stage. Around the person, and not around the email, the team keeps comments, to-dos, shared candidates and reminders. A hiring manager who opens the system once a quarter for one panel sees the same board the recruiter sees, narrowed to their role, and does not need a training session to find the next action.

### 5. Interviews
Scheduling runs against the interviewers' calendars, so nobody trades twelve emails to find an hour. Interview kits give everyone on the panel the same instructions, the same questions and the same scorecard. The point of that is comparison: the team compares candidates against each other on shared criteria, rather than comparing interviewers' moods.

### 6. Decision, offer, first day
Evaluations sit side by side when the panel meets, so the discussion starts from what each person wrote down before they heard the others. The offer is signed electronically through an integration. Before day one, the new hire gets onboarding tasks, and the handover to the HR system carries the details across.

### 7. Afterwards
The people who did not get the job do not disappear. With consent, and with a retention period that follows the country they applied in, they stay in a talent pool for the next opening. Analytics close the loop: time to hire, source of hire, stage conversion and drop-off, for one role or for the whole group. Those are the numbers the head of TA takes into the budget meeting, and they only exist if the process ran through the system.

## ATS, recruitment CRM, HRIS, talent suite: which is which
The labels overlap, and vendors use them loosely. Used strictly, they describe where a system starts and where it stops, which is the thing a buyer needs to know when two systems have to hand over to each other.
Term What it is Where it starts and stops
ATS The system that runs the hiring process for a job: applications, stages, interviews, decisions, the record. Starts when a role is requested. Stops at the signed offer, when the candidate becomes an employee.
Recruitment CRM Relationship tools for people who are not yet applying: talent pools, outreach, events, nurture. Starts before there is a job. In Teamtailor it is part of the same system, so a contact and an applicant are one record.
HRIS The employee record: contracts, pay, absence, org chart, reporting. Starts on day one. The ATS hands over to it. Teamtailor integrates with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors and Personio. [S12]
Talent suite or talent acquisition platform An ATS plus modules for onboarding, performance, learning or compensation, often from an HRIS vendor. Spans several stages of the employee lifecycle. One contract and one vendor is the upside. The recruiting module is rarely the part the vendor is proudest of, so test it on real roles before you accept it as part of the bundle.
Recruitment software The whole category, from job posting tools to full platforms. No fixed boundary. Treat it as a search term, not as a requirement.

### Where the HRIS boundary sits
In an enterprise, the rule that keeps this clean is simple: the ATS owns the candidate until the signed offer, and the HRIS owns the employee from then on. The integration is the handover of a short list of fields: name, start date, salary, manager and cost centre. Get those five agreed between TA and HR before the pilot, because most delays in a rollout are an argument about who owns a field.
The integration list is worth reading for what is on it and also for how it runs: whether the handover is triggered by a stage change, whether failed records are visible to the recruiter, and who gets the error. Ask to see it run on a real hire.

## What candidates see
The candidate sees a career site that loads quickly, a form that can be finished on a phone, a reply within days and a clear idea of what happens next. That is the part of the ATS your brand is judged on, and it is also where applications are lost without anyone noticing.
Phones carry more of this than many teams assume. In Teamtailor's hospitality benchmark, 46.9% of applications came from a phone. [S30] In retail it was 64.1%. [S31] Both figures are activity recorded in Teamtailor by its customers, so they describe those industries on this platform and not every employer. For an enterprise recruiting across shifts, sites or frontline roles, a form that only works well at a desk is a form that loses part of the pool.

### Replies, and what comes next
Most of what a candidate remembers is tone and timing. A message that says what happens next and when, even when the answer is no, costs a template and a trigger. Teamtailor includes a candidate survey and a candidate NPS, because you cannot improve what you do not measure, and because the people best placed to say how it felt are the ones who went through it.
What is automatic and what is not. Teamtailor does not score CVs on its own. Automation such as Smart move acts only on conditions a recruiter sets, and those can include CV keywords [S35] . The recruiter reads what was sent. What happens automatically is what the team configured in triggers, and the team can see it.

### Several brands, one candidate
A candidate who applies to one brand of a group should see that brand's career site, its voice and its privacy notice, not the group's ATS. In a multi-brand set-up, this is a requirement and not a cosmetic choice: the applicant has agreed to something specific, with a specific legal entity. How the platform separates brands is covered in the next section.

## The enterprise requirements
The security reviewer starts in the trust centre, where the certificates and reports are already published. The hiring manager in Lisbon logs in with the company account and never sets a password. The new entity in Poland opens its own career site, and the group's reporting still adds up. That is what a system built for enterprise buying looks like once it is running, and the table below is the checklist that gets you there.
Read it left to right: the requirement, why it matters at 1,000+ employees, what to ask any vendor, and where Teamtailor stands, with the source.
Requirement Why it matters at 1,000+ What to ask the vendor Where Teamtailor stands
Single sign-on (SAML 2.0) One identity per person, access removed when they leave, no password reset queue. Which identity providers are documented? Can SSO be enforced? Is it available per group of accounts? SAML 2.0 SSO, set up under Settings, then Security. Guides exist for Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin and Google. When SSO is enforced, password login is disabled. A parent account can run one setup for a group (Group SSO). [S5]
User provisioning (SCIM) Joiners, movers and leavers are handled by IT, not by a recruiter remembering. Which providers is it tested with? Users only or groups too? Who issues the key? Tested with Microsoft Entra ID and Okta. User objects only, groups are not supported. The key is issued by your Teamtailor contact. [S6]

Six standard roles and two that depend on an add-on: No Access, Default User, Hiring Manager (submits jobs as pending, cannot publish), Recruitment Lead, Recruitment Admin, Company Admin, Division Admin (only with Divisions) and External Recruiter (add-on). The regions operate separately, and no data is transferred between instances. [S4]

Three structures: one account; one platform with several career sites using Divisions (shared by default, selective separation, an own career site per division, a Division Admin role); or the Group solution, where a parent account connects separate child accounts, each with its own branding, settings and processes, no data shared between them, plus Group SSO and Group Analytics. Time to hire, source of hire, stage conversion, apply rate and drop-off, and custom reports that are shared without exporting. Group Analytics covers the Group solution. [S9]
Users and seats Per-seat pricing quietly stops hiring managers from getting access. Are users limited? Are job postings limited? Is the price per seat? Unlimited users and unlimited job postings. Pricing is per organisation, not per seat. [S13]
Support A hiring manager who cannot find a button on a Monday morning is not going to wait for a ticket. Who can contact support? Is there a named contact for large accounts? Live chat for every user, regardless of access level, and dedicated Customer Success Managers. [S12]
Accessibility and languages Career sites and application forms fall under accessibility law in many markets. Is there a conformance statement against WCAG? Which languages does the candidate flow cover? The European Accessibility Act applies from 28 June 2025, to services including websites. [S34] Ask Teamtailor, as any vendor, for the current WCAG conformance statement through the trust centre.
The audit log row is the one worth reading twice. The default retention is short, and longer retention costs extra, so the question for your security team is not whether the log exists but how far back it has to go.

### Questions for the security reviewer
- What is the date and scope of the latest SOC 2 Type 2 report, and were there exceptions?
- Which entities and products does the ISO certificate scope cover, and when was the last surveillance audit?
- Where is the sub-processor list, and how much notice do we get before it changes?
- Which data region will we be in, and what is processed outside it?
- What are the retention defaults, and can they differ by country?
- How long is the audit log kept, and what does a longer period cost?
- Can SSO be enforced for every user, so that password login is off?
- Does SCIM deprovisioning remove access immediately, and what happens to the candidate data the user owned?
- How often is the application penetration tested, and can we see a summary?
- How quickly does the DPA require you to notify us of an incident?

## Security certificates, read for a buyer
The security reviewer finds, in one document, the name of each standard, what it covers, what it leaves out and the date of the last audit. Most certificates say less than their badge implies, so each entry below gives what it certifies, what it does not, and what to ask for.
- ISO/IEC 27001
- Certifies an information security management system (ISMS): the policies, the risk process and the controls, audited by an accredited body. Certificates run three years, with annual surveillance audits. [S22] It does not say the product is free of bugs. It says the organisation manages security in a controlled way. Ask for the certificate, the scope statement and the date of the last surveillance audit.
- ISO/IEC 27701
- The privacy extension to ISO/IEC 27001, a privacy information management system (PIMS). It maps to the duties of a GDPR controller and processor. [S23] Ask whether its scope covers the product you are buying.
- ISO/IEC 27017 and ISO/IEC 27018
- Cloud-specific security controls (27017) [S24] and protection of personal data in public clouds where the provider acts as a processor (27018). [S25] They are usually held by the data-centre provider, not by the software vendor. Ask who holds them.
- ISO 22301
- Business continuity management. [S26] It is the certificate for the question of what happens when the data centre burns. Ask for the recovery targets in the contract, not only for the badge.
- ISO/IEC 42001:2023
- The first management-system standard for AI, published in December 2023. [S27] It certifies how an organisation governs the AI it builds and buys (risk assessment, roles, monitoring), not the model itself. [S27] It is relevant to readiness for the EU AI Act. Ask what the scope is and who audited it.
- SOC 2 Type I and Type II
- An attestation report under the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, and not a certificate. Type I describes the controls at a point in time. Type II tests that they operated over a period, typically six to twelve months. [S28] Ask for the Type II report, its period and any exceptions listed.
- CSA STAR
- The Cloud Security Alliance's registry, built on its cloud controls matrix, either self-assessed or certified. [S29] Ask which level the vendor holds, since the two carry very different weight.
- GDPR and the DPA
- GDPR is a law and not a certificate. "GDPR compliant" on a website means nothing until you have read the data processing agreement, the sub-processor list and the transfer mechanism.

## Where the assistance fits
The recruiter ends the day with a first draft where there used to be a blank page, and has still made every decision herself. That is the useful shape of the assistance in an ATS: it handles the first pass, and a person handles the judgment.
In Teamtailor, the system does these things:
- drafts a job ad from a few lines about the role;
- summarises a CV and a video interview;
- suggests interview questions for the role;
- answers scorecard questions from the interview transcript;
- evaluates candidates against criteria the team set;
- surfaces people from the talent pool who match a new opening.
Each of these is a draft or a suggestion in front of a person. The team reads the summary and decides whether it is right. The criteria for an evaluation come from the team, so the logic is theirs and not a hidden score.
That is also the shape the law asks for. As a deployer under the EU AI Act, an employer informs candidates, keeps human oversight and keeps logs. A system that suggests and a person who decides makes oversight a normal part of the day, not a separate process.

### What to ask the vendor
If a vendor says the system will decide for you, ask to see it decide. Then ask who is accountable when it is wrong, and where in the product that person can see why.

## Questions people ask

### What does ATS stand for?
ATS stands for applicant tracking system. It is the software where a hiring team runs the process for a job: applications, stages, interviews, decisions and the record afterwards. People also say recruitment software, which is the wider category. In an enterprise the ATS also carries permissions, privacy settings and reporting across several entities.

### What is the difference between an ATS and a recruitment CRM?
An ATS runs the hiring process once a job exists. A recruitment CRM manages relationships with people who are not applying yet: talent pools, outreach, events. Most buyers want both, and the useful question is whether they share one record. In Teamtailor they are part of the same system, so a contact and an applicant are one person.

### Does an ATS reject CVs automatically?
Only if the team sets it up. Teamtailor does not score CVs on its own. Automation such as Smart move acts only on conditions a recruiter sets, and those can include CV keywords, and the recruiter reads what was sent. What happens automatically is what the team configured in triggers, such as moving a candidate after a screening answer or sending a message. Ask any vendor to show exactly what runs without a person.

### Is an ATS GDPR compliant?
GDPR is a law, not a certificate, so no system is compliant on its own. The ATS has to support what you need to do: retention rules, consent handling, deletion that works and an audit trail. Read the data processing agreement, the sub-processor list and the transfer mechanism before you rely on a claim.

### Does an ATS support single sign-on and user provisioning?
Many do, but check the details. Teamtailor supports SAML 2.0 single sign-on, with guides for Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin and Google, and password login is disabled when SSO is enforced. User provisioning through SCIM is tested with Entra ID and Okta, and covers users but not groups.

### Where is candidate data stored?
It depends on the vendor, so ask for the region and where processing happens. In Teamtailor the customer chooses between Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. Europe is stored with AWS in Ireland, North America in Oregon and Asia-Pacific in Australia. The regions operate separately and no data is transferred between them.

### Is an applicant tracking system a high-risk AI system under the EU AI Act?
Recruitment and selection systems are listed as high-risk in Annex III of the EU AI Act, where they use the kind of functions the Act describes. After the Digital Omnibus, the high-risk obligations for Annex III apply from 2 December 2027. Employers that deploy such a system must inform candidates and keep human oversight and logs.

### Can several brands or companies share one ATS?
Yes, and the structure matters. Teamtailor offers one account, one platform with Divisions and a career site per division, or a Group solution where a parent account connects separate child accounts that share no data. Which fits depends on whether brands should share candidates, settings and reporting, or keep them apart.

### How long does an enterprise ATS implementation take?
It depends on the number of entities, integrations and countries, so be wary of a single number. Five Guys went from signature to launch in eight weeks across more than 1,700 restaurants. Knauf ran a two-year programme for 43,500 employees. Ask the vendor for a plan per phase, with names against each.

### What does an ATS cost for a company with 1,000 employees?
Vendors rarely publish prices, because they quote per company and the answer depends on the model. Compare what is included before the figure: users, job postings, modules, implementation and add-ons such as audit log retention. Teamtailor has unlimited users and job postings and is quoted per organisation, so ask for a figure through the pricing page.

### How do we migrate from an HRIS recruiting module to a dedicated ATS?
Start with the boundary: the ATS owns the candidate until the signed offer, and the HRIS owns the employee afterwards. Agree the fields that pass across, usually name, start date, salary, manager and cost centre. Then decide which historical candidate data is worth migrating under your retention rules, and run the first hires through the integration before rollout.

### Which are the best applicant tracking systems?
It depends on what you hire for and how many people are involved. A retailer with shift roles, a group with ten brands and a team of five recruiters need different things. List your requirements, then compare vendors against them. Our comparison pages put Teamtailor next to the systems you are probably also looking at.

## What an ATS does in recruitment
An applicant tracking system (ATS) is where a hiring team keeps the work of filling a role: the job, the applications, the stages, the interviews, the decisions and what was said to whom. The category is large. Jobscan, which looks at the careers pages of the Fortune 500, detected an ATS at 487 of 500 of them in 2026, or 97.4%. [S17] So when someone asks whether recruiters really use one, the answer is yes, and the more useful question is what the one in front of you does with a Tuesday.
This guide follows a role through the system, from the request to the record that is left afterwards. We make an applicant tracking system, so where we describe how a step works in Teamtailor we say "in Teamtailor", and where something is true of the category we say that instead. The detail comes from our support centre, linked at the end of the page, and not from memory.

### What it is not
An ATS is not the HR system. It owns the candidate until the offer is signed, and the HRIS owns the employee from the first day. It is also not only a database of CVs. A database remembers people. An ATS also knows who is waiting for whom, which is the part a recruiter opens it for at nine in the morning.
If you want the buying angle (security review, multiple entities, procurement), that is in our complete guide to applicant tracking systems . This one is about the mechanism.
A note on language. "Recruiting tracking system", "recruitment ATS" and "ATS recruitment" mean the same thing as an applicant tracking system. We use the full term and the abbreviation interchangeably.

## The pipeline: one board for every role
Everything else hangs on the hiring pipeline . Each job has stages, each candidate sits in one stage, and moving them is the unit of work. The stages differ from role to role, which is how a warehouse hire and a finance manager can share a system without sharing a process.

### Stages and stage types
In Teamtailor, a job starts from a pre-built process that the team can change, and stages are added in the job's editing mode. [S3] Each stage belongs to one of five types: Inbox, Screening, Interview, Offer or Hired. Inbox and Hired are fixed, and custom stages are placed under Screening, Interview or Offer. [S3]
The type matters more than the name. A stage called "Chat with Maria" and one called "Phone screen" can both be Screening, and the pipeline reports then count them together. The names are for the team, the types are for the numbers. Decide the types once, and a report of how many candidates reached the Interview type means the same thing across every job.

### What a recruiter sees at nine
The board is a list of people per stage, and the useful part is the edges of it: who has been in a stage longest, who has a to-do waiting, whose message has gone unanswered. The first thing a recruiter learns to read is the stage that is full on the left and empty on the right. That is a bottleneck with a name on it, and it is usually a person who is out of the office, not a candidate problem.

## Posting the job and receiving applications

### The job and its approval
In Teamtailor, a job is created from the Jobs tab with a title, department, role, locations, the main recruiter, the number of open positions and a recruitment period. [S4] A hiring manager submits a request, the job gets the status "Pending creation", and recruitment leads and admins are notified so they can create it. [S4] Where a hiring manager can create jobs, the access level does not include publishing: the job moves to pending and a recruitment lead or administrator publishes it. [S7] If the company uses the job approvals add-on, the job setup shows the approval flow that applies to the job. [S4]
This is the first place an ATS earns its keep for a bigger team. The approval is a state on the job, with a name against it, instead of a "yes" somewhere in a thread. Three weeks later, when someone asks who agreed to the extra headcount, you open the job and read it.
Two fields shape the rest of the process. The number of open positions decides when the job closes itself: the job switches to Completed once hires reach it, and no more candidates can be moved to Hired unless the number is raised. [S4] The recruitment period appears in the hiring plan, so progress is tracked against dates the team agreed. [S4]

### Where the ad goes
The ad lives on the career site , which in Teamtailor is built in a career site editor: default pages are generated automatically, custom pages are added by hand, and each page is made of content blocks, with design settings for fonts, logos and colours. [S13] Publishing also sends the job to the free channels the account has switched on: Google Jobs (not in all regions), Indeed and Glassdoor, and Jooble are activated by default, and others, such as Adzuna and Jora, can be switched on under Marketplace. [S11] Two details are worth knowing. Sending a job is not the same as the channel listing it, since the channel decides, and the support article says it takes 24 to 72 hours for jobs to appear on the free channels after they are published. [S11] The free channels are not included in a trial account, and every job needs a location to be sent. [S11]
A recruiter who posts at four o'clock and checks at five for the ad on Indeed has not found a bug. That is the 24 to 72 hours.

### Applying, and not applying yet
Applications arrive in the Inbox stage, with the answers to the questions on the form. There is a second route for people who are not ready. In Teamtailor, a visitor can use Connect to say they are interested without applying: they choose departments and roles, create a profile, and get a thank-you email and job alerts when a matching job is posted. [S8] They stay in the pool until the next opening fits. [S8] That is how a talent pool fills without anyone importing a spreadsheet, and it is the half of a candidate relationship management tool that sits inside the ATS.

## Screening: what is automatic and what is not
This is the chapter people search for when they type "can an ATS reject my CV". The honest answer is that it depends on what the team set up, and the team can read it back.

### Questions on the form
Screening starts with what you ask. Yes/No and range questions are always mandatory in Teamtailor, and follow-up questions can be shown or hidden depending on an earlier answer. [S19] The questions are where the facts a role depends on get collected: a right to work, a licence, a language, a shift pattern.
The question types are Choice, Date, File, Number, Range, Text and Video. [S19] Conditional logic works on Yes/No and Choice answers, in the application form and in the message tab of the candidate card. [S19] Two design habits follow. Use a Choice or Range question where a rule will read the answer, since a rule can compare a selected option and cannot compare a paragraph of prose. Keep Text and Video for what a person will read, because those answers are for the recruiter and not for a condition.

### Triggers and Smart move
A trigger runs when a candidate enters a stage. [S1] It can send a message, add a comment or a to-do, add or remove tags, share the candidate, send an interview invitation through Smart schedule, or move the candidate on. [S1] A company admin has to activate triggers in the add-on feature centre first, and the default delay is one minute after the candidate is moved to the stage. [S1]
Smart move is the trigger that matters for screening. It moves a candidate to another stage when they meet conditions you set: question answers, job offer status, resume keywords, location, referral status, tags, and screening criteria if the add-on is on. [S2] You can set several groups of conditions, and the first matching group is the one used, so their order is a decision. [S2] Three rules save an afternoon of confusion:
- A trigger only affects candidates who enter the stage after it was added. Existing candidates are not touched, with one exception: triggers that act on screening criteria also run for candidates already in the stage. [S2]
- Editing a trigger also only affects new arrivals, except again for screening criteria triggers, which re-run when their configuration changes. A change to a resume, location or answers does not move a candidate who is already in the stage, but a change in job offer status does. [S2]
- A delay can be added, and if the candidate moves on during the delay the trigger is cancelled. [S2]
The second rule is the one that produces the Tuesday message: "I changed the trigger and nothing happened to the people already in the stage." Nothing was supposed to. Move them by hand, or in bulk, once.

### Screening against criteria
Teamtailor also offers assisted screening, which needs an add-on that a company admin switches on. A user with editing rights to the job writes the criteria, or accepts criteria suggested from the job description, and each candidate is marked as meeting, not meeting or unclear. [S10] The support article describes the recruiter as the one who decides: a mark of meeting or not meeting is only set when there is enough information to support it, otherwise the candidate shows as unclear, and the result can be reviewed and changed by hand on the candidate card. [S10] The only automatic step it describes is an optional Smart move trigger that acts on the result. [S10] The glossary has the general term: candidate screening .
What to ask any vendor: show me everything that happens to a candidate without a person pressing a button, and show me where I can read it. If that list is short and visible, the system is doing what you asked. If it cannot be shown, treat that as the answer.

### Does the software reject people?
Not by itself. Jobscan's own write-up does not describe automatic rejection; it describes recruiters using the system to search and rank candidates, and says 76.4% of the recruiters in its own survey rank candidates by the skills in the job description. [S17] That matters, because the filter is a human decision made once and applied many times. A knockout question on the form, a keyword condition in a Smart move trigger and a screening criterion are all rules someone wrote. Bad rules reject good people quietly, and the fix is to read them as often as you read the job ad.

## Hiring managers and the rest of the team
A recruiter can run a pipeline alone. A hire needs at least one other person, and that is where most of the friction in recruiting sits.

### One view, narrowed to the role
In Teamtailor, a hiring manager is invited to a recruitment process, sees the invited jobs under the Jobs tab, and opens each to see its candidates by stage. [S7] On a candidate card they can handle comments, to-dos, interviews and messages, and read what the candidate submitted. [S7] There is a Job comments area for the hiring team to discuss the process, and a bulk select to message, move or assign a to-do to several candidates at once. [S7]
The point of this is where the conversation lives. A comment on the candidate card stays with the candidate. A reply-all stays with whoever was copied. The difference shows when the hiring manager who was on holiday comes back and wants to know what happened to "the one with the Python project". They open the card.

### Comments with a visibility setting
Comments on a candidate go to anyone with access to that candidate, and comments on a job application go to the hiring team and admins. A comment can be restricted before it is posted, and a restricted comment shows a padlock. Company admins can see all comments. [S23] Files can be attached to a comment and then also appear under Documents on the profile, though executable file types are blocked. [S23] That is a small thing until a hiring manager sends a work sample by email and it is the only copy.

### Mentioning, restricting, sharing
Colleagues can be mentioned in comments and are notified according to their own notification settings. [S23] A candidate profile can be shared outside the account by link or email, with sections left out, personal details anonymised and a password set. Individual links can be revoked, and an admin can revoke all share links at once under Data & Privacy. [S20] Up to 20 profiles can be shared in one email. [S20] For sensitive roles, a candidate can be restricted so that only admins, recruitment admins and recruitment leads with access can open the card. [S22] The principle is the same as the approvals: put the permission where the person works, not in a rule people are asked to remember.

## Interviews, scorecards and the decision

### Booking the interview
Smart schedule picks meeting times that work for you and your team and sends the candidate options to choose from, and it can also be used as a trigger. The same support video covers sending meeting invitations to several candidates at once. [S18] That is the replacement for the exchange of "does Thursday work" messages, and the saving is not in the minutes. It is in the candidate not waiting two days for a reply while the recruiter waits for an interviewer.

### Interview kits and scorecards
An interview kit is a structured guide: instructions, the skills and traits to assess and the questions for them. [S6] In Teamtailor, a kit can be attached to a stage, and it then appears on the candidate card and is preselected when a meeting is booked for that stage. [S6] Reviewers must submit their own feedback before they can see their team members', which the article says is meant to reduce bias. The instructions added to the kit appear first when feedback is given, and an admin can link a kit to a stage, which helps when a job uses several. [S6] There is more on how this looks on our interview kits page .
The scorecard is the other half. Each skill or trait is rated from 1 to 5 with an optional comment, colleagues' evaluations can be read alongside your own, and ratings of 3 or higher are saved to the candidate's profile as competencies. [S5] The design choice to notice sits in the kit, not the scorecard: the submit-first rule. A panel that writes before it talks produces four independent opinions, where a panel that talks first produces one opinion repeated four times.

### Comparing the shortlist
For the decision, up to 50 candidates can be compared at once in side-by-side columns that include ratings, stage, tags, comments, interview kit feedback, skills and traits and answers to application questions. [S15] Candidates can be pinned to stay in view while you scroll, hidden from the comparison, and moved to the next stage or rejected from their column. [S15] Questions of the file and video types are not supported in the comparison, so keep the facts a decision rests on in Choice, Number or Range questions. [S15] It is a plain feature, and it is the one that ends the meeting where someone says "I thought we had agreed on her".

## What the candidate sees
Every step above has a candidate on the other side of it. The system decides how much of the process they can see.

### Status and messages
In Teamtailor, transparent recruitment lets connected candidates see a status for each application: unread, inbox, in progress, hired or rejected. [S14] They see "In progress" and not the exact stage, and a company admin turns the feature on and can disable it per job. [S14] The statuses are Unread, Inbox for an opened application still in the Inbox stage, In progress, Hired and Rejected, shown on the candidate's Connect dashboard. [S14] Messages go out from the candidate card or from triggers, so the "we have received your application" and the "we are not moving forward" are templates the team wrote once, not a favour someone remembers to do.
Candidate experience is mostly this: what the person was told, and when. A reject message sent three days late is remembered longer than a perfect careers page.

### Keeping data, and letting go of it
An ATS also decides how long people stay in it. Automatic data deletion in Teamtailor is configured under Settings, Data & Privacy. Rules cover inactive candidates, rejected applications, candidates with no active purpose, removal requests and missing or expired permission. [S9] A candidate who meets a rule is flagged and removed a week later, and the removal cannot be restored. [S9] Hired candidates can be excluded, and an add-on sets rules per country. [S9] On the legal side, the system gives you the controls, and the retention period is still your decision.

## Reporting, integrations and security

### The numbers that come out
If the process runs through the system, the system can report on it. Recruitment reports in Teamtailor cover pipeline progress and conversion between stage types, average days to hire and to fill, hires by source and department, meetings booked, candidate NPS and reject reasons. [S16] The pipeline overview takes a daily snapshot of where candidates sit by stage type, and the conversion report shows a funnel with the drop-off points. [S16] This is why the stage types matter: the pipeline reports count by type, so two jobs with differently named stages still report the same way. [S3] Reject reasons are the quiet one: the breakdown is only as useful as the reasons the team chooses when it rejects, so agree the list before the first rejection. See reporting and recruiting metrics .

### Integrations
An ATS sits between job boards, assessments, calendars, e-signing and the HR system. Teamtailor's integrations page states 550+ integrations, grouped into tools (including assessments, HR systems and background checks) and job boards and social media. [S12] The questions that matter are about how a handover runs, not how many there are: what triggers it, whether the recruiter can see it fail, and who gets the error. Browse the integrations to see what is there.

### Security
The trust centre lists GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and says Teamtailor ATS is audited annually under SOC 2 Type 2. [S21] Read the scope of any certificate before relying on it, and ask for the date of the last audit. The longer checklist is in the complete guide.

## Choosing an ATS, and next steps
There is no honest "best ATS for hiring", because the best one is the one your hiring managers open without being asked. The practical test is a real role, run through each system you are considering, with the hiring manager in it.

### A test you can run in an afternoon
- Take a live role with a hiring manager who dislikes software, and have them submit it, comment on two candidates and leave feedback on an interview.
- Build one screening rule and ask the vendor to show everything it did, and to whom.
- Book an interview from the card and watch what the candidate receives.
- Pull the reject reasons and the time per stage for that role.
- Ask for the list of what happens to a candidate's data a year after rejection.

## Questions people ask

### What is an ATS in recruitment?
An ATS, or applicant tracking system, is the software where a hiring team runs the work of filling a role: the job, the applications, the stages, the interviews, the decisions and the record afterwards. It sits between the career site and the HR system. It owns the candidate until the offer is signed, and the HRIS owns the employee from day one.

### Do recruiters really use ATS?
Yes. Jobscan detected an ATS at 487 of the Fortune 500 companies in 2026, which is 97.4%.<sup><a href="#source-S17">[S17]</a></sup> The other 13 may use a system built in-house. Recruiters use it to search, rank and move candidates between stages, and to keep comments, interviews and messages in one place.

### Can an ATS reject my resume?
Only if someone configured it to. Jobscan's write-up describes recruiters searching and ranking, not software rejecting by itself.<sup><a href="#source-S17">[S17]</a></sup> A knockout question, a keyword condition or a screening criterion is a rule a person wrote. In Teamtailor, the recruiter reads what was sent, and what runs automatically is what the team set up in triggers.<sup><a href="#source-S2">[S2]</a></sup>

### How do I pass my resume through ATS?
Send a plain document with ordinary headings, use the words the job ad uses for the skills you really have, and answer the application questions fully, since those answers are often what a rule reads. Skip text inside images and tables. A recruiter still opens the file, so write it for a person first.

### Which ATS is best for hiring?
The best one is the one your hiring managers open without being asked. Test with a real role: have a hiring manager submit it, leave feedback and compare candidates, then pull the reject reasons and time per stage. We make Teamtailor, so treat our view as one input. Our comparison pages show where we think the differences are.

### What are the top 5 ATS systems?
There is no neutral top 5, since lists differ by company size, country and what is being measured. Teamtailor is ours, so we do not rank it. For a shortlist, pick tools companies of your size actually use, and run the same real role through each. Our comparison pages put Teamtailor beside Greenhouse, Lever, Workable and others.

### What is the difference between an ATS and a recruitment CRM?
An ATS runs the hiring process once a job exists. A recruitment CRM manages people who are not applying yet, through talent pools and outreach. The useful question is whether they share one record. In Teamtailor, a person who used Connect to show interest can later apply, and the team sees one candidate.<sup><a href="#source-S8">[S8]</a></sup>

### How long is candidate data kept in an ATS?
As long as the company decides. In Teamtailor, automatic deletion rules cover inactive candidates, rejected applications, removal requests and expired permission. A flagged candidate is removed a week later and cannot be restored.<sup><a href="#source-S9">[S9]</a></sup> Retention periods follow your legal advice and the country the candidate applied in, not a default.

## Decide what the system is for before you see a demo
The shortlist is usually settled by the third demo, and the person who settled it often cannot say why. A feature that looked good in a sandbox with six invented candidates won over a feature nobody tested with four hundred real ones. The fix is dull and it works: write down what the software has to do, for whom, before any vendor is allowed to show you anything.
This guide is for talent acquisition teams who already know what an applicant tracking system (ATS) is and are choosing one, or replacing one. It covers the requirements worth writing down, the kinds of ATS software on the market, how to judge integrations and pricing models, and the questions that separate a demo from a deployment. It comes from a company that makes one, so where we describe how something works, we say it works that way in Teamtailor, and where a point applies to every vendor, we say that instead. If you want the category explained from scratch, the complete guide to applicant tracking systems does that, and the glossary entry for applicant tracking system is the short version.

### Four groups of users, four sets of requirements
A buying decision goes wrong when it is made on behalf of one of these groups only. List what each of them needs from the system, in their words, and keep the list on one page.
- Recruiters live in the pipeline all day. They need to find a candidate fast, move twenty people at once, message in bulk without it feeling like bulk, and see what is waiting on them.
- Hiring managers open the system a few times a month, usually between two other things. They need to see their own role, read what the recruiter wrote, leave a score and be done. If they have to be trained, they will not use it, and the process moves back into email.
- Candidates never chose the software, but they judge your company by it. The career site, the application form on a phone and the first reply are theirs.
- IT, security and legal decide whether the purchase happens at all. They want single sign-on, a data processing agreement and a clear answer on where the data is.

### Write down the process you actually run
Take the last three roles you filled and trace each one: where the request came from, who approved it, where the ad was published, how many applied, who screened, how many interviews, how the offer was made, what happened to everyone else. Differences between the three are the interesting part. A role that took eleven emails to schedule one interview tells you more about requirements than any feature list, because it names the step where the current tools lose time.
Bring the three traced roles to every demo and ask the vendor to run one of them. A scripted demo shows what the product does best. A role you picked shows what it does on a Tuesday.

## The kinds of ATS software on the market
Searches for "ATS software" return a single list, as if the products were interchangeable. They are not. The category has a few distinct shapes, and the shape matters more than any individual feature, because it decides what the vendor is good at and what it treats as an afterthought. Recruitment software is the wider term and has no fixed boundary, so use it as a search term and not as a requirement. The glossary entry for recruitment software sets out how the labels overlap.

Only the first bucket is allowed to rule a vendor out.

### What changes at 100 employees and what changes at 5,000
For a company of a hundred or so, the weight sits on speed to value: can two recruiters be live in a few weeks, is the career site good without a developer, is the price something the finance lead can approve alone. For a company of a few thousand, the weight moves to governance: several brands or countries, approval chains, single sign-on, a security review that takes a week and not a quarter. The same product can serve both, but the questions you spend demo time on should differ. The page for small and midsize teams and the page for enterprise show how we frame each.

## Integrations: read the list, then watch one run
The integration count on a vendor page is a poor guide, because it counts everything from a free job board to a deep two-way connection with an HR system. What you need to know is narrower: which five or six connections your process depends on, and how each one behaves when something goes wrong. An ATS integration that works in a demo and fails silently on a hire is worse than none, because the recruiter thinks the record has moved.

### The connections most teams depend on
- The HR system. The ATS owns the candidate until the signed offer and the HRIS owns the employee after that. The integration carries a short list of fields across: name, start date, salary, manager, cost centre. Agree who owns each field before the pilot.
- Job boards and social channels. Check which are included and which cost extra, and whether sponsored placements are bought inside the system.
- Assessments and interviews. Skills tests, video interviews and reference checks are where candidates leave the system and come back.
- E-signing and background checks. Offers and checks need an audit trail, so they should be triggered from the pipeline and not copied in by hand.
- Calendars and messaging. If interview scheduling does not read the interviewers' calendars, the saving you were promised disappears.

### What Teamtailor lists
The integrations page states 550+ integrations, and the product page describes them as making the hiring stack feel like one system. [S4] [S3] Read on the day we checked it, the page shows 80 HR systems, 127 assessments, 26 background-check providers and 16 e-signing tools, among other categories. [S4] HR systems named on the page include Bamboo HR, Dayforce, Hibob, Deel and Cezanne HR, and e-signing tools include DocuSign and Adobe Acrobat Sign. [S4] Counts on a directory move from week to week, so use them to see what kinds of connection exist and check your own HR system by name, with a vendor, before it becomes a requirement.
Ask three things about each integration you rely on. Is it triggered by a stage change or by a person? Can the recruiter see a failed record? Who gets the error message? The answer to the third is often nobody.

## Pricing models, and what to ask besides the price
ATS vendors charge in a handful of ways, and the model matters more than the headline number, because it decides who gets access and what you pay when the business changes. We have not put prices for other vendors in this guide. They change, they depend on the quote, and a figure we could not source would be worse than none.
Model How it grows Ask
Per user or per seat With the number of people who log in. Do hiring managers count as seats? If they do, expect access to be rationed, and the process to drift back to email.
Per open job With the number of roles live at once. How are evergreen roles and high-volume postings counted? What happens in a busy month?
Per employee With company headcount. Is it headcount of the whole group? Does it change when you acquire a company?
Flat or per organisation With the size of the contract, not the usage. What is the limit on entities, career sites or locations?
Base plus add-ons With every module you turn on. Which features in the demo are add-ons? What is the audit log, SSO or sandbox retention worth in the quote?

### How Teamtailor prices
Teamtailor does not publish prices. The pricing page asks for a few details about your company and answers with a quote. [S2] What it does state is that job postings and users are unlimited, that customer support covers all users, and that integrations and an open API are included. [S2] Two features are marked premium on the same page: requisitions and approval flows, and divisions and multi-brand management. [S2] The page also lists AI support across hiring as included, with unlimited usage. [S2] If you need either premium feature, say so in the first conversation so that the quote starts from your set-up.
Whatever vendor you speak to, ask for the three-year total, the renewal terms, what the quote assumes about the number of users and sites, and what happens to your data if you leave. The exit question is the least asked and the one a finance team will remember. The pricing page is where to begin with us.

## Security, access and data location
The security reviewer should be able to close the review from documents, not from a call with a sales rep. Look for a public trust centre, a data processing agreement, a sub-processor list and a certificate with a stated scope and date. A badge on a footer is not evidence.

### What Teamtailor publishes
- The trust centre lists GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 under compliance. It states that the ISMS and PIMS of the Teamtailor ATS and Aboard HR are certified under ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701, and that Teamtailor is independently audited annually under the SOC 2 Type 2 standard. [S1]
- Controls listed there include audit logging, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, application penetration testing, data retention periods, data erasure, incident response and an SLA statement. [S1] The page lists the control areas without describing how each is implemented, so ask for the document behind any you rely on.
- Single sign-on runs through SAML 2.0, and admins can enforce it for all users once the set-up is confirmed. External Recruiters are always excluded. [S6]
- Data can be placed in Europe (Ireland), North America (Oregon) or Asia-Pacific (Australia). Stored and processed locations differ per region, and the support article states that no data is transferred between instances while noting that personal data may still be transferred outside these areas depending on the services and sub-processors involved. [S7]
- Six roles run from No Access to Company Admin, with Division Admin and External Recruiter as add-on roles. [S8]

### Several brands or countries
If you hire for more than one brand, subsidiary or country, how the system separates them is a core requirement. In Teamtailor, divisions are for companies with multiple brands, business units, branches or subsidiaries. They share everything by default, with selective separation, and each division can have its own career site on its own URL. [S9] Ask every vendor the same: what is shared, what can be separated, whether a candidate sees only the brand they applied to, and whether you can still report across all of it.
For the detail on certificates and the rules that touch recruiting software now, the complete guide has a chapter on each, including a list of questions for the security reviewer.

## What candidates will see, and why it is part of the buying decision
A buying team looks at the recruiter's screen for most of an evaluation and at the candidate's for about ten minutes. That ratio is the wrong way round. The candidate's side is where your employer brand meets the software, and it is where applications are lost without anyone noticing, since nobody records the person who closed the tab.
Apply to one of your own jobs in the vendor's sandbox, on a phone, on the train, without telling anyone. Count the screens. See whether you can upload a CV from the phone's files, whether the form remembers anything and what you receive afterwards. A reply that says what happens next and when costs a template and a trigger; a vendor who cannot show you that has not thought about the person on the other end. Candidate-facing parts are covered in more detail in career sites .

### Automation and who decides
Automation is where buyers should be most careful with their wording. Ask what runs on its own, who configured it and where a recruiter can see what happened. In Teamtailor, triggers apply the same steps to every candidate when an event occurs, and the page recommends starting with one or two bottlenecks such as scheduling or emailing, keeping candidate names and job titles in messages, and tracking time to hire, NPS and conversion to refine them. [S5] More on this in recruitment automation and triggers . Whatever vendor you choose, a rule you cannot read is not a rule you can defend to a candidate or a regulator.

## Running the evaluation
An evaluation that goes well is shorter than one that goes badly. Give each step a person and a deadline, and add time for the security review, the data processing agreement and works council consultation where those apply.
- Long list of five to eight. Filter on the must-have bucket only. Ask for the trust centre link and the integration list before a call is booked.
- Short list of three. Give each vendor the same brief: one of your traced roles, your HR system, your approval chain.
- A sandbox for one live role. Run a real role with a real hiring manager, even if only as a rehearsal. A hiring manager who gets stuck on the first screen is the most useful result you will get.
- Reference calls. Ask for a company of your size and your industry, and ask what they would change about the first ninety days.
- Security and legal in parallel, not after the choice. A review that starts once you have picked takes the vendor's side of the negotiation away from you.
- Decision on a scorecard, filled in by each member of the group before you discuss it.

### A scorecard that keeps the discussion honest
Criterion Weight Scored by
Recruiter workflow on a real role Highest Recruiters who ran the sandbox
Hiring manager can use it unaided High The hiring manager from the pilot
Candidate experience on a phone High Someone outside the team
Integration with the HR system, run on a test hire High HR operations and IT
Security, privacy and data location Pass or fail Security and legal
Reporting you will take to the budget meeting Medium Head of talent acquisition
Three-year cost and exit terms Medium Finance and procurement
The weights are a suggestion. What matters is that they are agreed before the first demo and that the "pass or fail" row is one that can really stop a deal. If your group is split on the scorecard, that is useful: it usually means two stakeholders had different jobs in mind, which is better found now than at go-live. A common thing to find is that the hiring manager score decides the pilot, since a system the managers will not open is a system whose reports cannot be trusted.

## Twenty questions to ask every vendor
These work as an agenda for a demo and as a checklist for a written response. Ask them in the same order to each vendor and write the answers down.

### About the product
- Can you run one of our traced roles, from request to signed offer, in front of us?
- What can a hiring manager do without a recruiter, and what is blocked?
- Where does the career site live: inside the system, or connected from outside?
- Which actions can run automatically, and where can we see what ran?
- How are candidates who did not get the job kept, and for how long, by country?

### About integrations and data
- Which integrations are native and which are maintained by a third party?
- What triggers the handover to our HR system, and who sees a failed record?
- Is there an open API, and is it documented publicly?
- What can we export, in what format, and what happens to our data when we leave?
- Which data region will we be in, and what is processed outside it?

### About security and compliance
- Where is the trust centre, and what is the scope and date of each certificate?
- When was the last SOC 2 Type 2 report, and were there exceptions?
- Can single sign-on be enforced for every user, and how are leavers removed?
- How long is the audit log kept, and does a longer period cost extra?
- Which of your features are designed for the rules on AI in recruitment, and who audits the claim?

### About the contract and the people
- What does the price assume about users, sites and job volume?
- Which features in this demo are add-ons?
- What does onboarding include, and who is our named contact?
- What are the renewal terms and notice period?
- Which customer of our size would you put us in touch with?

Teamtailor is built around one idea: the recruiting work, the career site and the conversation with hiring managers are in the same system, so the team is not stitching them together. ## Questions people ask

### What is ATS software?
ATS software is an applicant tracking system: the program where a hiring team runs the process for a job. It holds the job, the applications, the stages, the interviews, the decisions and the record afterwards. Many systems add a career site, messaging and reporting. Recruitment software is the wider term, and the two are often used for the same thing.

### What are the top 5 ATS systems?
We have not ranked them. A top five means little until it is set against your requirements: company size, volume, HR system, countries and budget. Our comparison pages go through individual products side by side, written to be fair to the other vendor, and the requirements table in this guide gives you the criteria to rank them yourself.

### How do I pass my CV through ATS?
A CV does not pass or fail an ATS in one step. The system stores the application and shows it to people, and the employer decides what is automated. Use a plain layout, standard headings, the wording from the job ad where it is true, and answer the screening questions fully. Applying from a phone should work without creating an account.

### What is the best ATS tool?
The one that fits your process, your size and your stack, so we do not name one. Teamtailor is our own product, and we think it fits many teams, but the evidence is your own pilot. Trace your last three roles, write down the must-haves and make each vendor run one of those roles before you decide.

### What are the top 10 ATS?
We have not written a top ten, because a ranking only means something against your own requirements. A better route is a long list of five to eight that meet your must-haves, a short list of three, and a pilot on a real role. The comparison pages cover several widely used products one at a time.

### What are the most common ATS used by companies?
We cannot give a figure we can source, so we do not claim one. Usage differs by company size and region: the products common among small teams differ from those at large employers. For your own market, ask peers and reference customers of your size which systems they run and what they would change.

### What is an ATS in healthcare?
It is an applicant tracking system used by healthcare employers, with the same core as any other plus requirements specific to the sector: licence or registration questions at application, shift and location filters, volume across many sites, and careful handling of candidate data. Ask a vendor to show screening questions that move a candidate on based on the answer.

### What is the most popular ATS software?
We do not have a sourced popularity figure, so we do not name one. Popularity also says little about fit: a product common at large employers may be wrong for a team of 120. Judge by your requirements, ask for references from companies of your size and run a pilot on a real role.

### How much does ATS software cost?
It depends on the model: per user, per open job, per employee, a flat fee or a base plus add-ons. Teamtailor does not publish prices and gives a quote after you describe your company. Its pricing page states unlimited users and job postings.<sup><a href="#source-S2">[S2]</a></sup> Ask every vendor for the three-year total and the renewal terms.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a structured interview?
A structured interview is one where the interviewer comes prepared with a set of standardized questions that are asked of every candidate for the role. The questions are asked in the same order, with the same follow-up questions and the responses are ranked on the same scale and criteria.

### Why is a structured interview important?
Structuring interviews makes it easier for the interviewer to prepare and provides a better experience for the candidate. Deciding the questions in advance makes the process consistent and fair, no matter who's running the interview, and increasing the likelihood of getting all the information the hiring team needs to make the right decision. By standardizing the evaluation process, it's then easier for the hiring team to identify the right candidate for the role.

### How to structure an interview?
The first step to creating a structured interview is setting expectations within the hiring team. What general instructions do they need to follow to ensure a great candidate experience and a consistent process for every interview? Then you can work on the actual structure, setting the questions you'll ask every candidate. Finally, make a list of all the skills and traits that the ideal candidate would bring to your company.

### What is an Interview Kit?
Teamtailor's Interview Kits help hiring teams create and conduct structured interviews. By gathering general instructions, essential questions, the skills and traits you're looking for, and a candidate scorecard all in one place that's easily accessible by the whole team, you can ensure you're hiring the right candidate while streamlining the hiring process.

### How to conduct a structured interview?
You've done all your prep, now it's time to meet the candidate! Begin with a friendly greeting before diving into your prepared questions. Ask them in order, being sure to give the candidate plenty of time to respond thoughtfully to each one. Make sure to listen carefully to their answers and begin to think about how you might grade their response. Once you've asked everything in the plan, close the interview, and fill out their scorecard, while the information is still fresh in your mind. With Teamtailor's Interview Kit, you can even fill out the score card during the interview for immediate and seamless assessment.
