## What recruitment software is
Recruitment software is any system that carries part of the hiring process: posting the job, receiving applications, moving people through stages, booking interviews, collecting decisions and keeping the record. The term is a search term more than a product class. It covers a plugin that posts to job boards just as well as a platform that runs a whole hiring organisation, and a vendor who says "recruitment software" has told you almost nothing yet.
This guide is written for talent acquisition teams who already know what a requisition and a pipeline are. It sorts the category into the parts that matter when you choose, describes what each part does across one hire, and lists what to ask before you sign. It is written by a company that makes one, so where we describe how something works we say "in Teamtailor", and where a point holds for every vendor we say that instead.

### Recruitment software, recruiting software, hiring software
The three phrases are used interchangeably. British and Australian sites tend to say "recruitment software" and American ones "recruiting software". "Hiring software" is the same category under another name. In practice they point to the same shelf. The useful distinction is not the name but the job the tool does, which is the next chapter.
Figures in this guide carry a marker that points to the source list at the end of the page. Pages were read on 29 October 2026, and vendor claims, including ours, are described as claims.

## The categories inside the category
When two vendors both say "recruitment software", they are often selling different things. The table sorts the common types by the job they do and by where they start and stop, which is what decides how many of them you will end up running side by side.
Type What it does Where it starts and stops Typical gap
Applicant tracking system Runs the process for a job: applications, stages, interviews, decisions, the record. Starts when a role is requested. Stops at the signed offer. Often weak before the application, when people are still deciding whether to apply.
Recruitment CRM Holds relationships with people who are not applying yet: talent pools, outreach, events, follow-up. Starts before there is a job. Needs a link to the ATS, or a person exists twice with two histories.
Career site builder Publishes the jobs and the story of working at the company. Starts when someone lands on your page. If it sits outside the ATS, the form and the pipeline stop sharing data.
Job posting and multiposting tools Send one ad to many boards. Stops once the application is submitted. Applications still need a home.
Interview, assessment and scheduling tools Book time, run structured interviews, test skills. Covers one or two stages. Results have to flow back to the candidate record.
HRIS recruiting module A recruiting feature inside the employee system. Starts from the employee record, so the hiring process often feels like an afterthought. Test it on a real role before accepting it as part of a bundle.
Recruitment platform Combines several of the above in one system. Spans attraction to onboarding. Breadth varies a lot, so read the feature list, not the label.
Most teams past a handful of hires a year end up with an ATS at the centre and a few tools around it. The decision that matters is how many of those tools you want to keep in sync by hand. The glossary entries on recruitment software and talent acquisition software give the short versions of the terms.

## What the software does across one hire
The clearest way to see what recruitment software is for is to follow one role from request to first day. This is how that runs in Teamtailor. Other systems order the steps differently, but the same jobs have to be done somewhere, and the question for a buyer is whether they happen in one place or in five.

### The request and the ad
A recruiter at a regional retailer opens a request from a store manager who has typed "need two people for weekends" and nothing else. The first job of the software is to turn that into a job with a title, a location, screening questions and an approver, so the person who says yes is on the record. In Teamtailor the ad is built from a few lines about the role and edited by a person, then published to the career site and to job boards from one place.

### Applications
Candidates apply from a phone, often without an account. Those who are not ready to apply can leave their details instead, so the team can come back when a fitting role opens. In Teamtailor that is the Connect function on the career site, which lets candidates show interest even when no suitable role is open. [S5]

### Screening and the first decisions
Screening questions are set per job: right to work, a licence, shift availability. Triggers then handle the routine part. In Teamtailor a trigger runs when a specific event happens, for example when a candidate applies or answers a screening question, and it can send a message, prompt a hiring manager or create a follow-up task. [S4] What happens automatically is what the team configured. The recruitment automation entry explains the idea, and the automation and triggers page shows it in the product.

### Interviews and evaluations
Scheduling should not cost twelve emails to find an hour. Teamtailor lists Smart Scheduling among what the ATS includes. [S11] Interview kits are made up of interview instructions, relevant questions and a scorecard, and the whole hiring team can open them. [S10] The point is comparison: the panel compares candidates on shared criteria rather than comparing interviewers' impressions.

### Offer and handover
The offer is sent for e-signature, usually through an integration, and the details move to the HR system once the candidate becomes an employee. See e-signature and offer management for what each step should cover. In Teamtailor the integration directory lists e-signing and HR systems as categories of their own. [S3]

### Afterwards
The people who did not get the job do not have to disappear. With consent, and a retention period that fits the country they applied in, they stay in a talent pool for the next opening. Reporting closes the loop: time to hire, source of hire and stage conversion. Those numbers only mean something if the whole process ran through the system, which is the argument for keeping the steps together.

## When a spreadsheet and an inbox stop being enough
Almost every team starts without recruitment software. A shared inbox, a spreadsheet with a column for "status" and a hiring manager who replies when they can. It works until the day it does not, and the day has a recognisable shape: someone is on holiday and nobody knows who was promised a call back.
The usual triggers for a first purchase, or for a replacement, are these.
- Volume. A single role that draws a few hundred applications makes the inbox unworkable, and answering everyone becomes a task of its own.
- More than one decision-maker. Once several hiring managers need to see candidates, sharing attachments by email becomes a data protection question as well as an irritation.
- Several locations or brands. Each needs its own career site and its own jobs, and the group wants the numbers together.
- Proof. Someone asks how long hiring takes, where candidates come from, or why a person was rejected a year ago, and the answer has to come from a record.
- A system that no longer fits. Aptitude Research reports that 82% of organisations say their current system has significant functionality gaps, and that 1 in 4 companies were replacing their ATS in 2025. [S7] The survey is about the ATS, but the same drift shows up in any tool that was bought for a smaller company.
The same research notes that nearly half of enterprise companies manage more than one ATS platform. [S7] That is the cost of buying tools one at a time. It is easier to choose how things connect before you have six of them.

## What to look for when you compare
Feature lists in this category look alike, because every vendor can tick the same boxes. The differences sit in how the parts fit together and who in the company can actually use them. We would compare on seven points, and we describe each as it works in Teamtailor so you can hold any vendor, including us, to the same questions.

### 1. One place for the work
Count the tools a single hire touches today: job board logins, the inbox, the calendar, a spreadsheet, an e-signature tool, the HR system. Each hand-off between them is a place where data is retyped or lost. The aim is not to have one tool for everything, but to know which system holds the truth about a candidate at every stage. In Teamtailor, talent pools and candidate CRM sit inside the ATS rather than beside it; see candidate relationship management . [S11]

### 2. The career site
The career site is where the candidate decides. In Teamtailor it is built inside the system with drag-and-drop blocks and without involving a web team, it can show Team Stories from employees, and pages can be translated per language. [S5] The point to test in any vendor is whether the site and the pipeline share data, or whether you maintain both. See the career site and employer branding pages for how we do it.

### 3. Hiring managers
The most common reason a system fails is that the hiring managers do not use it. They open it a few times a quarter and will not learn a new interface for it. Look for one board narrowed to their roles, a clear next action, and comments and decisions that stay on the candidate instead of in an email thread. Ask to see a hiring manager logging in for the first time, with no training.

### 4. Integrations
No recruitment software stands alone. The Teamtailor integrations directory states 550+ integrations, with categories that include assessments, background checks, video interviews, e-signing, HR systems and onboarding, plus job boards and social media. [S3] Treat any such number as a starting point: ask which ones you need, how they are built, and what happens on the recruiter's screen when one fails. The integrations page has the list.

### 5. Automation you can read
Automation saves time when the team can see what it does. A rule such as "when a candidate answers the licence question with no, send this message" is easy to audit. A black-box score that decides who is seen is not. Ask every vendor to show exactly what runs without a person, and who configured it.

### 6. The candidate's side
A candidate sees a page that loads, a form that works on a phone, a reply and an idea of what happens next. In Teamtailor, triggers can send a tailored thank-you message when someone applies and survey candidates at set moments. [S4] Check the same for any vendor: what does a candidate get on day one, on day five and on rejection?

### 7. Security and records
Candidate data is personal data. Teamtailor states that it is ISO 27001 and 27701 certified and audited to SOC 2 Type 2 annually, [S2] and its trust centre lists the certifications and reports. [S1] For any vendor, ask for the scope statement and the date of the last audit, because a certificate can cover the organisation without covering the product. Also ask for single sign-on and an audit log. In Teamtailor, single sign-on uses SAML 2.0 [S8] and the audit log records the date, time and actor of key actions, with a default retention of 15 days that can be extended manually up to 30. [S9]

## Which is the best recruitment software
People who search for recruitment software often type "best" in front of it, and the results are lists of ten or twenty names. A list is a fair place to start looking for names and a poor place to decide, because the question hides a missing requirement. A retailer hiring shift workers, a software company hiring engineers through referrals and a group of ten brands with a works council in two countries need different things from the same category.

### Write the requirements first
Before you open a list, write down the five things that would make you reject a vendor. For most teams of 100 to 5,000 employees they come from this set: the number of hires per year, the number of brands or countries, the HR system you must connect to, the security evidence procurement will ask for, and the hiring managers who must use it. A shortlist of three vendors that meet all five is more useful than ten names that meet some.

### Then test on a real role
Ask each vendor to set up one of your open roles during the demo, with your screening questions and your approval chain. Watch who touches the keyboard. A system that only works when the vendor drives it will only work when the vendor is there.

### Where to read comparisons
We have written comparison pages that put Teamtailor next to other applicant tracking systems, among them Greenhouse, Workable, Recruitee, SmartRecruiters and Lever. They are written by us, so read them with that in mind and check each claim against the vendor's own site.

## Cost, contracts and what can go wrong
Pricing models differ more than prices do. Some vendors charge per user, some per job posting, some per company, and some by a bundle of modules. A per-user model looks cheap for five recruiters and becomes a reason not to invite hiring managers at fifty. In Teamtailor, pricing is quoted per organisation; the pricing page explains how to get a figure.

### What to compare besides the figure
- Users and job postings: whether hiring managers count as paid users.
- Modules: whether the career site, the CRM and onboarding are included or sold separately.
- Implementation: who does the work, and how long they say it takes.
- Add-ons: log retention, additional data regions, premium job boards.
- The exit: how you export candidate data if you leave.

### The risks that show up later
Three come up again and again. The first is that the recruiters like the tool and the hiring managers do not, so decisions move back to email. The second is data that was never cleaned before migration, so the new system starts with duplicates. The third is automation set up by one person who then leaves, so nobody knows why a candidate received a message. All three are preventable with an owner, a clean-up and a written list of the triggers that run.
Benchmarks help you judge your own process, though they describe other organisations. SHRM's 2026 recruiting benchmark, with data from over 4,600 organisations, reports a median time-to-fill of 39 calendar days for nonexecutive positions. [S6] Measure your own before you compare.

## The first ninety days
Buying recruitment software is the smaller job. Getting a team to use it is the larger one, and the first ninety days decide it.

### Days 1 to 30: one team, a few real roles
Pick one team that hires often and has a hiring manager who wants it to work. Set up their open roles, their screening questions and their approval chain. Import only the candidate data you would still be allowed to keep under your retention rules, and leave the rest in the old place. Name one owner in TA who decides how stages and triggers are set up, because a system with six owners has six pipelines.

### Days 31 to 60: connect the neighbours
Connect the HR system, the calendar and the e-signature tool, and run the first real hires through the handover. Agree which fields pass to the HR system: usually name, start date, salary, manager and cost centre. Most delays at this stage are an argument about who owns a field, so settle it before the first offer.

### Days 61 to 90: the rest of the company
Roll out to other teams with a short routine for hiring managers, not a training course. Switch on reporting and look at the same three numbers every month: time to hire, source of hire and stage conversion. The reporting page shows what Teamtailor records, and the article on recruitment analytics goes through how to read them.

## Next steps
If you are early in the process, write down your five rejection criteria, list the tools a hire touches today, and ask each vendor to run one of your roles in the demo. If you are replacing a system, start from the data: what you will export, what you will keep and who owns the clean-up.

## Questions people ask

### What is the best recruiting software?
There is no single best, because the answer depends on how many hires you make, how many brands or countries you cover, which HR system you connect to and who has to use it. Write five rejection criteria, shortlist three vendors that meet them and test each on one of your own open roles. Our comparison pages show Teamtailor next to common alternatives.

### What are the best recruitment software tools?
The tools worth shortlisting depend on the job. An applicant tracking system sits at the centre, with a recruitment CRM for people who are not applying yet, a career site, and integrations for interviews, assessments and e-signature. Judge each by how it connects to the others and whether hiring managers will use it, not by the length of its feature list.

### What are the top 10 recruiting platforms?
A top ten changes with the author, the year and the size of company in mind, so we do not publish one as fact. What holds across lists is the type: platforms that combine applicant tracking, a career site and a candidate database. Use a list for names, then compare on your own requirements and ask each vendor to run a real role.

### What are the top 5 ATS systems?
Rankings depend on who is asking, so we do not rank. We publish <a href="/en/comparison/">comparison pages</a> that put Teamtailor next to other applicant tracking systems. They are written by us, so check claims against each vendor's own site and test on a real role.

### What does recruitment software do?
It carries the hiring process for a job: the ad, the applications, screening, stages, interviews, decisions, the offer and the record afterwards. Better systems also hold a talent pool for later openings and report on time to hire, source of hire and stage conversion. The aim is to keep the work in one place instead of in an inbox.

### What is the difference between recruitment software and an ATS?
An applicant tracking system is one kind of recruitment software, the kind that runs the process for a job from request to signed offer. Recruitment software is the wider category and also includes recruitment CRM, career site builders, multiposting and interview tools. Many platforms now combine them, so read the feature list rather than the label.

### Do small companies need recruitment software?
Not at the start. A shared inbox and a spreadsheet work for a few hires a year. The need appears with volume, several hiring managers, more than one location or the first question about where candidates come from. When a team has reached at least one of these, it is time for a system.

### How much does recruitment software cost?
It depends on the model: per user, per job posting, per company or by module. Compare what is included before the figure, including whether hiring managers count as users, and what the exit looks like. Teamtailor is quoted per organisation, so ask for a figure through the pricing page.

### Is recruitment software secure?
It depends on the vendor, so ask for evidence. Teamtailor states ISO 27001 and 27701 certification and annual SOC 2 Type 2 audits, with documents on its trust centre. For any vendor, ask for the scope of each certificate, the date of the last audit, single sign-on and an audit log, and read the data processing agreement.

When implemented well, it speeds up shortlisting, reduces bias, and improves the quality of candidates reaching the interview stage.

# What is Application Conversion Rate?
Teamtailor
Teamtailor
Application conversion rate is the percentage of career site visitors who complete and submit a job application. It is calculated by dividing the number of completed applications by the total number of unique visitors to your job listings, then multiplying by 100. This metric reflects the effectiveness of your career site, job listings, and application process at converting interest into action.

A low application conversion rate means you are attracting candidates but losing them before they apply. Common causes include lengthy application forms, required account creation, poor mobile experience, unclear job descriptions, or a career site that fails to sell the opportunity. Even small improvements in application conversion rate can significantly increase your candidate volume without spending more on sourcing .

# What is a Background Check in Recruitment?
Teamtailor
Teamtailor
A background check is a verification process conducted on a job candidate before finalising a hire. It may include criminal record checks, employment history verification, education verification, reference checks, credit checks, and social media screening. The scope of background checks varies by industry, role, and jurisdiction. They serve as a final due diligence step to confirm that the candidate has been truthful and meets the requirements for the position.

## Why it matters
Background checks protect organisations from negligent hiring claims, reduce the risk of fraud or misconduct, and verify that candidates are who they say they are. In regulated industries like finance, healthcare, and education, certain checks are legally required. However, background checks must be conducted fairly and consistently, in compliance with local laws (including GDPR in Europe), to avoid discrimination and protect candidate rights.

# What is Boolean Search in Recruitment?
Teamtailor
Teamtailor
Boolean search is a technique used by recruiters to create precise candidate searches using logical operators AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. For example, searching for (developer OR engineer) AND Python NOT junior narrows results to experienced Python developers or engineers. Boolean search is used on LinkedIn, job boards, ATS databases, and any platform with search functionality to find specific candidate profiles efficiently.

## Why it matters
Sourcing without Boolean search is like searching the internet without knowing how to use quotation marks. You get too many irrelevant results and miss the candidates you actually want. Boolean operators let recruiters combine keywords with precision, dramatically improving the quality and relevance of search results. For technical roles or specialised positions, Boolean search is an essential sourcing skill that separates effective sourcers from those who rely solely on basic keyword searches.

A competency-based interview is a structured interview format where questions are designed to assess specific skills, behaviours, and attributes required for the role. Instead of asking hypothetical questions, competency-based interviews ask candidates to provide real examples from their past experience that demonstrate the target competency. For example: Tell me about a time you had to manage a conflicting priority. The STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) is commonly used to structure answers.

Past behaviour is the best predictor of future performance. Competency-based interviews focus on what candidates have actually done rather than what they say they would do in a hypothetical scenario. This produces more reliable, objective evaluations and reduces the impact of candidates who interview well but lack real substance. For hiring teams, it standardises evaluation across interviewers and makes it easier to compare candidates fairly.

# What is Hiring Bias?

Teamtailor
Hiring bias is any prejudice, conscious or unconscious, that influences hiring decisions based on factors unrelated to a candidate's ability to perform the job. Common forms include affinity bias (preferring people similar to you), confirmation bias (seeking information that confirms initial impressions), halo effect (one positive trait influencing overall assessment), horn effect (one negative trait overshadowing everything else), and name or demographic bias.

## Why it matters
Bias in hiring leads to less diverse teams, poorer hiring decisions, legal risk, and missed talent. It is pervasive because human decision-making is inherently subjective. The goal is not to eliminate bias entirely, which is impossible, but to design processes that minimise its impact. Structured interviews, anonymised screening, standardised criteria, diverse interview panels, and data-driven evaluation all help reduce bias and lead to fairer, better hiring outcomes.

A streamlined requisition process accelerates time-to-fill ; a cumbersome one delays it.

# What is Offer Acceptance Rate?

Glossary

# What is Offer Acceptance Rate?
Teamtailor
Teamtailor
Offer acceptance rate is the percentage of job offers extended by an organisation that are accepted by candidates. It is calculated by dividing the number of accepted offers by the total number of offers made, then multiplying by 100. A healthy offer acceptance rate varies by industry and role type, but generally falls between 85% and 95%.

## Why it matters
A low offer acceptance rate wastes significant recruitment effort and budget. Every declined offer means restarting the process, often after weeks or months of sourcing , screening, and interviewing. Common reasons for declined offers include uncompetitive compensation, slow hiring processes (the candidate accepted another offer), poor candidate experience , or a misalignment between what was promised and what was offered. Tracking this metric helps identify and fix the root causes.

## How Teamtailor helps
Teamtailor helps improve offer acceptance rates by speeding up the hiring process (so you do not lose candidates to faster competitors), providing a great candidate experience throughout, and giving you analytics to understand where and why offers are being declined.

A panel interview is an interview format where a candidate is interviewed by multiple people simultaneously, typically including the hiring manager , a peer, an HR representative, and sometimes a senior leader or cross-functional stakeholder. Each panellist evaluates the candidate from their own perspective and area of expertise. Panel interviews provide a more comprehensive assessment in a single session compared to sequential one-on-one interviews.

## Why it matters
Panel interviews are efficient because they compress multiple evaluation perspectives into one meeting, reducing the number of interview rounds and accelerating time-to-hire . They also reduce individual bias since no single interviewer controls the evaluation. However, panels can be intimidating for candidates if not managed well. The key is preparation: each panellist should have defined questions and a clear role, so the interview feels like a conversation rather than an interrogation.

## How Teamtailor helps
Teamtailor's interview kits support panel interviews by assigning specific question sets and evaluation criteria to each panellist. After the interview, all feedback is collected in one place for a holistic candidate view.

It also makes the actual first day far more productive because administrative tasks are already handled and the new hire feels expected and welcomed.

Quality of hire is a recruitment metric that evaluates the value a new employee brings to the organisation after being hired. It is typically assessed through a combination of performance reviews, hiring manager satisfaction, time-to-productivity , retention rate, and cultural fit. Unlike metrics that measure process efficiency ( time-to-hire , cost-per-hire ), quality of hire measures the outcome, whether the hiring process actually resulted in good hires.

Optimising for speed and cost alone can lead to poor hires that cost far more in the long run. A bad hire can cost up to 30% of the employee's annual salary when you factor in recruitment costs, training, lost productivity, and eventual replacement. Quality of hire is the ultimate measure of whether your recruitment strategy is working. Tracking it forces organisations to look beyond vanity metrics and evaluate whether the people they are bringing in are actually performing and staying.

# What is a Recruitment Agency?
Teamtailor

A recruitment agency (or staffing agency) is an external firm that helps organisations find and hire candidates for open positions. Agencies typically work on a contingency basis (paid only when a hire is made) or retained basis (paid an upfront fee for a dedicated search). They maintain their own candidate databases, conduct sourcing and screening, and present shortlisted candidates to the hiring organisation. Agencies are most commonly used for hard-to-fill roles, executive search, or when internal recruitment capacity is limited.

## Why it matters
Agencies can be valuable for specialised or urgent hiring needs, but they are expensive, typically charging 15-25% of the hire's annual salary. Over-reliance on agencies significantly inflates cost-per-hire and means the organisation is not building its own recruitment capability. The most effective strategy is to use agencies selectively while investing in internal recruitment infrastructure (ATS, employer brand, sourcing skills) that reduces agency dependency over time.

## How Teamtailor helps
Teamtailor includes external recruiter portals that let agencies submit candidates directly into your pipeline with appropriate visibility controls. This keeps all candidates in one system while reducing the administrative overhead of agency management.
